stackfacts/keywords: watch my stack for end-of-life and new exploited CVEs
Use when you need to know what changed in a stack since your last check
what changed since my last check
alert when a version reaches end of life

description: Check dependencies, runtimes and OS versions for what changed since your last call: EOL passed or near, new OSV advisories, new CISA KEV hits. Returns a token.

inputSchema.description: Send either the stack (items, cves, packages, warn_days: starts a watch) or a token from the last answer (token, full: a re-check), not both

cves.description: Optional CVE ids to check against CISA KEV; duplicates are merged. Leave out (or send []) to check versions only

full.description: Re-check only: also return data.check, the full current stack answer, at the same price (default false)

items.description: The versions to check, in order: "product@version" strings or {product, version} objects. Needed unless packages is sent. Send each item as one string, product@version, e.g. {"items":["nodejs@18.19.0"]}

product.description: endoflife.date product id or alias, e.g. nodejs, python, ubuntu (GET /v1/eol/index lists them)

version.description: Version string, e.g. 18.19.0 (send "3.10" as a string, not a number)

packages.description: Optional package URLs with versions, answered as POST /v1/osv/check answers them (advisories, fixed versions, KEV flag). Types: npm, pypi, golang, cargo, maven (nuget, gem and composer are answered as ecosystem_unavailable until imported)

items.description: purl with a version, e.g. pkg:npm/lodash@4.17.20 or pkg:maven/org.apache.logging.log4j/log4j-core@2.14.1

token.description: Re-check only: data.watch.token from your last answer. Nothing else with it but full. It holds your stack in readable form; keep it as you would the stack

warn_days.description: Start only: report an item as due soon when its EOL date is this many days away or fewer (default 90, 0 = off). Kept in the token

name: stackfacts_stack_watch
